publicationStmt.p: This student digital edition of selections from La Police de Paris Dévoilée is designed to connect modern students and researchers interested in the history of policing, the French Revolution, and the organization of state power with an eighteenth‑century firsthand account of administrative authority in Paris. The selections presented here offer an accessible entry point for readers who may be unfamiliar with obsolete French, including language learners, and who wish to engage with primary documents without reading the entire work. Through robust indexing and the addition of contextual footnotes, this edition aims to clarify references, explain historical institutions, and highlight patterns in the text’s treatment of surveillance and public order.

normalization.p: In this publication, spelling was modernized for ease of contemporary readers. Each instance of modernized spelling will be tagged with the choice element, and the original and regularized spellings will be listed using "orig" and "reg".

punctuation.p: Punctuation has not been regularized as it does not meaningfully impede textual comprehension. The editors have done their best to transcribe punctuation exactly as it appears in the text, which entails inconsistent patterns of spacing before/after punctuation marks.

interpretation.p: Sentence construction and other grammatical aspects were left as found in the original to best maintain the voice of the author and avoid divorcing the text from the temporal context in which it emerged.
